correctness.rationale: For a star, the source connected-subgraph theorem gives exactly m leaf facets and \(2^m\) center-containing facets. Their intrinsic projected normal lengths are respectively \( eta_m\) and \(lpha_m\). Summing all leaf clearances gives \(x_0\le1-mr eta_m\), while averaging all center-containing clearances gives \(x_0\ge2rlpha_m-1\), yielding the sharp upper bound. The displayed center attains equality in every facet. At an optimal radius, equality in both aggregate inequalities forces every individual facet inequality to be tight; comparing subset facets then forces \(x_i=y_i\), proving center uniqueness.

value.rationale: Cosmological polytopes are a canonical graph-indexed family connecting convex geometry with the wavefunction-of-the-universe construction. The star family already has exponentially many facets, so the result is structurally stronger than evaluating a small fixed polytope: it proves that all \(2^m+m\) facets are simultaneously tangent for every dimension and gives the unique center and exact radius. This complements the existing face, triangulation, volume, and vertex-shell theory with a natural Euclidean invariant and an all-facet contact phenomenon.
